title: 0219 - THE PAIR-LAW MARRIAGE TEST (LOOM-1b2a, OFF-BOARD, no RH claim): the pair law (measured 2-consecutive-gap bias as an order-1 Markov generator, fit at each scale) vs the REAL H3 ladder, 3 alphabets x 3 scales (2e6/1e7/1e8) - SPLIT VERDICT, itself the finding: (1) the LANE word (L8, the M1 prediction machine's own alphabet, the owner's 'out of order' 24-adic lane) is MARRIED to the pair law at 1e7 (D=-0.0398 ~2SE) and 1e8 (D=-0.0004, 0.04 SE, PERFECT): the 2-gap bias is a COMPLETE description of everything the lane process does beyond the pair, at scale; the 2e6 lane excess (0.1886, 7.2SE) is finite-scale bias-in-transition; (2) the FINER gap-class words are NOT subsumed by the pair law EVEN AT 1e8: A6 D=-0.1456 (35.6 pooled SE, persistent) and G24 (gap class mod 24, 12 symbols) D=-0.1295 (8.9 pooled SE), but the G24 excess DECAYS with X: -0.4461 -> -0.2077 -> -0.1295 (roughly halving per decade) - the deeper weave lives in the fine 24-adic gap resolution that the lane word averages away, and either (a) decays away (slow-bias / finite-scale residue) or (b) is exactly the LD/LO k-tuple k>=3-gap correlation - the part of the sieve law genuinely beyond any pair model; the two horns are separated by G-1 (is the decay just mip-blur through a widening lens) and G-3 (can a tail-trained variable-context NN earn the residual from the tail); (3) Cramer memoryless floors sit well above all (A6 Cramer H3 1.72-1.75 vs real 1.35-1.39; lanes Cramer ~1.98-2.06 vs real 1.74-1.98): the pair law captures ALL the lane-memory, the gap-class residual is the measured object beyond it; sanity (the fit marries the pair part by construction): model H1/H2 match real H1/H2 within ~2SE at every cell; caveats: order-1 model H_m is a plug-in estimator on 1.0M-symbol chains (de-biasing widens the real-model gaps, so 'deeper' verdicts are CONSERVATIVE); the pair law here is EMPIRICAL at each scale, not the theoretical LO asymptote - the LD k-tuple joint generator (LOOM-1b2b) is the final adjudicator
body: Owner (0219): 'let's do the pair law and let these two get married already!' (a follow-up to 0218's LM1: real H3 was ~7SE below the EMPIRICAL order-2 floor at X=2e6; the question was whether the pair law, properly fit, explains the full weave). Executed as scripts/sq/loom4_pair_law_marriage.py (output tmp/loom/loom4_out.txt; 201.7s single-threaded, 4 cores open). Method: at each X in {2e6, 1e7, 1e8} and each alphabet - L8 = the 8 reduced LANES (p mod 24 in {1,5,7,11,13,17,19,23}, the M1 machine's alphabet), G24 = gap class mod 24 (12 even symbols, the full 24-adiic gap loom), A6 = gap/2 mod 6 (the LM1 word) - measure (a) REAL H1/H2/H3 per-symbol entropy (8-block Markov fit, block SE), (b) the CRAMER memoryless floor (iid at the empirical marginal), and (c) the PAIR-LAW MODEL: fit the measured order-1 (pair) transition matrix at THIS scale (Laplace +1), generate 5 synthetic 1.0M-symbol chains from the fitted matrix, H1/H2/H3 of the chains. Marriage test at H3: |real - model| <= ~2 pooled SE => MARRIED (the pair law explains beyond-the-pair too: subsumed); real below model by >2 SE => the weave is DEEPER than the pair law. RESULTS (full): X=2e6: L8 real H3=1.7386+/-0.026 model 1.9273 D=-0.1886 (7.2SE, deeper, finite-scale); G24 real 1.6283 model 2.0744 D=-0.4461 (20.6SE, deeper); A6 real 1.3501 model 1.5231 D=-0.1730 (15.0SE, deeper). X=1e7: L8 real 1.9160 model 1.9558 D=-0.0398 (~2SE) MARRIED borderline; G24 real 1.8966 model 2.1043 D=-0.2077 (9.3SE, deeper); A6 real 1.3782 model 1.5302 D=-0.1520 (24.1SE, deeper). X=1e8: L8 real 1.9832+/-0.013 model 1.9836 D=-0.0004 (0.04 SE) MARRIED PERFECT; G24 real 2.0037 model 2.1332 D=-0.1295 (8.9SE, deeper, decaying); A6 real 1.3919 model 1.5375 D=-0.1456 (35.6SE, deeper, persistent). Cramer floors: L8 ~1.98-2.06, G24 ~1.92-2.32, A6 1.72-1.75. Reading: (1) LANES marry: the prediction machine's alphabet carries NO structure beyond the 2-gap bias at scale - the 'out of order' next-24-adic-lane problem (L2A: M1 0.2205 top-1) is, at 1e7/1e8, exactly its own pair law; the 2e6 lane excess is the bias still transitioning (consistent with L1b: the bloom decays with X). (2) G24/A6 do not marry even at 1e8: the fine 24-adiic gap-class process has a persistent beyond-the-pair memory (A6: -0.146 = 35.6SE at 1e8 is the most confident single number of the loom program so far). (3) The G24 excess decays ~halving per decade (-0.446 -> -0.208 -> -0.130): two horns remain - (a) a slow-law / finite-scale residue (decays to zero, e.g. an LO-type 1/ln X bias in the 3-gap correlation) vs (b) the LD/LO k-tuple law's genuine k>=3 correlation (a fixed non-zero asymptote that an order-1 model can never capture; note an order-1 Markov CANNOT represent 3-gap structure by construction, so a persistent G24 excess is EXPECTED for real primes and the question is its SIZE vs the LD prediction and its scale form). Separators: G-3 (NN baby model: if a tail-trained variable-context model earns the residual from the tail => deep learnable memory, consistent with an LD k-tuple law; if it saturates at the pair level => the residual is not in the tail => slow-law/bias) and G-1 (splat/mip: if the decay is footprint blur through a widening lens, the 'true' gap-class asymmetry is flat, not decaying). CAVEATS (honest): the model H_m is a plug-in entropy estimator on short chains - a true order-1 process has H3=H2=H1, but the plug-in reads the model H3 slightly low (fewer samples per high-order context); de-biasing the model UP makes the real-model gaps WIDER, so every 'deeper' verdict here is conservative; the empirical pair matrix at each scale is not the theoretical LO asymptote (the asymptote would use a single fixed pair law at all scales; using the local fit is the generous choice for the model). Bug-free run (the loom3 bug fixes - axis=1 cumsum, per-run seeds - carried over). All off-board, no RH claim anywhere; lane lane lane: this is the second consecutive clean marriage test (0218 LM1, 0219 pair law) pointing at the same object: the fine 24-adic gap-class process is where any structure BEYOND the sieve pair law would have to live, and G-1/G-3 are the two named instruments that can tell 'new object' from 'known slow law'.
